SEC Amendment 30 of December 9, 2004 restructured the Abigail Trust, moving 3.3 million shares into Trust 600 and 3.75 million directly to Wexner [Finding #1525]. Kaufman, an attorney and shareholder of Kaufman Peterson and Dishler PC at 315 East Hyman Avenue, Aspen, Colorado, "succeeded as sole trustee of each of Trust 600 and R.H.R.E.I. Trust" [Finding #1510][SEC:0000909518-07-000835]. The filing did not name Epstein as the predecessor trustee or explain the succession [Finding #1510]. Trust [Finding #2493][EFTA00300480]. The presence of inter-entity transfer documents inside Epstein's storage indicates Epstein retained control records for transfers among Wexner-linked entities including YLK, COUQ/WCOUQ, and Buckeye LLC [Finding #2493].

Wexner Sale of Nine East 71st Street Corporation to NES, LLC" with full closing documents — a Nominee Agreement, Stock Power, Stock Certificate, Assignment and Assumption Agreement, Promissory Note, Guaranty, and "LHW Resignation" — alongside a general ledger dated September 30, 1998 [Finding #2493][EFTA00300480]. The structure of the Manhattan transfer used a corporate stock sale and nominee arrangement rather than a real estate deed transfer between principals, with Wexner resigning as director of the corporation rather than executing a direct conveyance to Epstein [Finding #2493]. Cross-reference of the 1989 acquisition deed (Wexner Columbus address), the 2011 deed (Epstein-associated Manhattan address), and the 2021 USVI-to-London transfer chain indicates the 9 East 71st property passed through Wexner-controlled, Epstein-controlled, and offshore-controlled corporate holders before its 2023 arms-length sale [Finding #1514].

sections.title: Legal Proceedings
sections.content:
The Limited was named as a defendant in the January 13, 1999 Saipan garment-industry class actions filed in the District of the Northern Mariana Islands [Finding #2344][CL:18838563]. The lead case, DOE 001 v. Advance Textile Corp (1:99-cv-00002, filed January 14, 1999), was a class action against 26 manufacturers and 23 U.S. retailers; a parallel case, Doe I v. The Gap (1:01-cv-00031), alleged a 13-year RICO enterprise under 18 U.S.C. 1962 [Finding #2358][CL:18838563][CL:18885284]. The complaints alleged peonage, indentured servitude, and international-law violations affecting more than 30,000 garment workers [Finding #2344][Finding #2358]. The Limited's 10-K for FY2000 confirmed The Limited as a named defendant; the FY2002 10-K and a Gap Inc. 8-K dated September 26, 2002 documented an $11.25 million settlement from 23 manufacturers and 7 retailers, granted conditional preliminary approval on October 31, 2002 [Finding #2344][Finding #2358][SEC:0000093066-02-003385]. The sourcing structure underlying the cases ran through Mast Industries Inc, a wholly-owned Limited subsidiary that handled 35 percent of merchandise, and Mast Industries (Far East) Ltd, a Hong Kong subsidiary; Mast had $329 million in external sales in FY2002 and the Limited's foreign sourcing income reached $69.7 million in FY2000 [Finding #2344].

In May–June 1999, Delaware Chancery Court shareholders filed a derivative action against The Limited's board seeking to rescind a Contingent Stock Redemption Agreement with Leslie H. Wexner and the Wexner Children's Trust [Finding #2389][SEC:0001021408-00-001562]. The shareholders alleged self-dealing in an arrangement that would have permitted Wexner to redeem stock at guaranteed prices [Finding #2389]. The derivative action was filed in the same window as the Saipan class actions [Finding #2389].

SHANKS v. WEXNER (E.D. Pa. 2:02-cv-07671, filed October 2, 2002, terminated October 21, 2003) was a diversity breach-of-contract case before Judge Clarence Charles Newcomer in which Leslie Wexner, Abigail Wexner, Jeffrey E. Epstein, and Ghislaine Maxwell were named as defendants alongside portrait artist Nelson Shanks [Finding #1358][CL:11742516]. The case is the documented joint legal proceeding involving all four parties [Finding #1358]. Separately, House Oversight deposition transcript HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_022159 records Lawrence Summers's former colleague Alan Dershowitz testifying that he telephoned Abigail Wexner to convey his view that an "extortion plot" was directed at Leslie Wexner; Dershowitz's testimony states that Abigail responded the Wexners "are aware of that they have already been in contact with us" [Finding #1532][HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_022159]. The deposition predates the related Virginia Roberts Giuffre litigation; Dershowitz's framing is self-attributed and Giuffre's testimony documents separate allegations [Finding #1532].

sections.title: Philanthropic and Political Activity
sections.content:
Wexner co-founded the Mega Group with Charles Bronfman in the 1990s, a network of Jewish-American philanthropists that included Ronald Lauder, Edgar Bronfman Sr., and Michael Steinhardt [Finding #1531][LittleSis:4432:rel1634429]. Wexner also chaired the Board of Trustees at Ohio State University from December 2005, served on the Dean's Council at the Harvard Kennedy School, and was a director of Sun-Times Media Group from 1996 to 2002 (the Hollinger International / Conrad Black ownership period) [Finding #1531][LittleSis:4432]. His wife Abigail Wexner, née Koppel, was an associate at Davis Polk and Wardwell in New York and London from 1987 to 1992; her father Yehuda Koppel opened the first El Al Israel Airlines ticket office in New York in the 1950s [Finding #1379][LittleSis:80089].

The Wexner Family Charitable Fund (EIN 31-1318013) was established in 1991 at 8000 Walton Parkway, Suite 100, New Albany, Ohio, and held $140.7 million in assets as of 2023 [Finding #1519][990:311318013]. The fund's Form 990 revenue was $170.7 million in 2014, $254.4 million in 2021, and $129.9 million in 2023; assets grew from $87.7 million in 2011 to $184.9 million in 2021 [Finding #1519][990:311318013]. The Wexner Foundation (EIN 23-7320631) maintained $10–15 million in annual revenue and $3–6 million in assets across the same period and functioned as the operating foundation for leadership-development programming, while the Family Charitable Fund served as the endowment vehicle [Finding #1519][990:237320631]. Comparison of Form 990 revenue spikes (2014, 2021) against Wexner's SEC Form 4 disposition dates indicates a temporal correlation between L Brands stock sales and charitable-fund inflows [Finding #1518][Finding #1519].

Wexner Form 4 filings (CIK 901359) document a multi-year liquidation of L Brands holdings [Finding #1518]. Wexner held 58.98 million shares (14.4 percent) in 2005 and reduced this position systematically: 1.55 million options exercised in April 2017; 509,000 shares disposed in October 2017; 1.13 million shares disposed in December 2016; gifts and sales totaling 5 million shares in August 2020 (after the COVID stock collapse from approximately $80 to $30); 5.05 million shares in March 2021 at $58.31; 8.5 million in June 2021 at $65.30; and 39.76 million shares in July 2021 at $73.01, the largest single transaction, timed to the L Brands / Bath & Body Works spinoff [Finding #1518][SEC:0000909518-21-000001]. Total dispositions across 2020–2021 exceeded 40 million shares, valued at approximately $2–3 billion at the recorded prices [Finding #1518]. FEC records show 515 contributions, predominantly Republican and Ohio-focused, with $100,000 donations to Right to Rise USA (Jeb Bush, 2015), With Honor Fund (2017), Buckeye Leadership Fund (2024), and Fighting for Ohio Fund (2016); Right to Rise USA in 2015 is the only $100,000 recipient shared with Leon Black in the Epstein-associated donor set [Finding #463][FEC:C00570549/schedule_a]. Personal lobbying was limited to five filings between 1999 and 2003 — two on apparel and trade and three on Wexner Heritage Village budget items — with all later lobbying conducted through L Brands corporate entities [Finding #420][LDA:44a141fd-5da1-4fee-bc21-e64fd5c510de].
